cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still speaking to the people, and he's just listed the blessings that come with obeying the LORD (Deuteronomy 28:1-14). Now he flips the cookie over. If they do not obey the LORD their God, he says, curses will come upon them and overtake them.
Cursed in the city and cursed in the country. Even the basket and the kneading bowl will be cursed, and friend, the kitchen is MY department.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the curse reaches Israel's children, crops and animals too.

cards.text: Cursed coming in and cursed going out. Then Moses says the LORD will send curses, confusion and reproof.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will send curses, confusion and reproof on Israel. How much of their work will it touch?

answers.text: Everything they put their hand to
Their fields but not their homes
Their homes but not their fields

cards.question: Moses says the curses will keep coming until Israel is destroyed, because of the wickedness of ___ the LORD.

cards.text: Next comes sickness and drought: Moses says the LORD will make a plague cling to them and strike them with wasting disease, fever, scorching heat, drought, blight and mildew. Then he says, "The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron."

cards.question: With a sky like bronze over them, what does Moses say the LORD will turn the rain of their land into?

cards.text: Then war. Moses says the LORD will cause them to be defeated before their enemies.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says Israel will march out against their enemies in one direction and send those enemies fleeing in seven.
Defeated before their enemies, what does Moses say Israel will become to all the kingdoms of the earth?

cards.text: Moses says their bodies will be food for the birds and the beasts, with no one there to scare them away.
Moses keeps going: the boils of Egypt, tumors, scabs and itch that can't be cured, plus madness, blindness and confusion of mind. At noon they'll grope about like a blind man in the darkness.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says that when Israel is oppressed and plundered day after day, someone will come to save them.

cards.text: Then comes a list of things they'll start but never get to keep. Moses says a man will be pledged in marriage to a woman, but another man will violate her.

cards.question: Next on that list of things they'll start but never keep, Moses says a man will build a house. What will happen?

answers.text: He will not live in it
It will burn to the ground
It will fall in a storm

cards.question: True or false: Under the curse, a man who plants a vineyard will enjoy its fruit.

cards.text: Moses says a man's ox will be slaughtered right in front of him, and he won't eat any of it. His donkey will be taken, and his flock will be given to his enemies.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says their sons and daughters will be given to another nation while their parents look for them day after day.

cards.text: Moses says a people they don't know will eat the produce of their land and all their toil. Then he comes back to boils, painful and incurable, from the soles of their feet to the top of their head.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will bring Israel and the king they appoint to a nation neither they nor their fathers have known. What will they worship there?

answers.text: The LORD in a new temple

cards.text: Among the nations the LORD drives them to, Moses says they'll be scorned and ridiculed.

cards.question: Moses says they will sow much seed in the field but harvest little, because the ___ will consume it.

cards.text: Moses says worms will eat the grapes, and the olives will drop off the trees. Plant it, water it, wait on it, and it'll never make it to the table.

cards.question: Moses turns to the foreigner living among Israel. Under the curse, what does he say will happen to that foreigner?

answers.text: He will rise higher and become the head
He will leave the land for good

cards.text: All these curses will chase them down and overtake them until they're destroyed. Moses says they'll be a sign and a wonder on them and their descendants forever.

cards.question: Moses gives a reason for all of this. In all their abundance, what does he say Israel did not do?

answers.text: Serve the LORD with joy and gladness
Share their riches with the poor
Build a great temple for the LORD

cards.question: Because they didn't serve the LORD with joy, Moses says they will serve their ___ in famine, thirst, nakedness and destitution.

cards.text: Now Moses describes an enemy. The LORD will bring a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, to swoop down on them like an eagle.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says Israel will understand the language of the nation from the ends of the earth.
Moses calls the nation from the ends of the earth ruthless. How does he say it will treat the old and the young?

answers.text: No respect for the old and no pity for the young
Respect for the old but no pity for the young
Pity for the young but no respect for the old

cards.text: Moses says they will eat the offspring of Israel's livestock and the produce of their land, and leave them no grain, new wine or oil.

cards.question: Moses says the ruthless nation from far away will besiege every city in Israel's land. What will finally fall?

answers.text: The high fortified walls they trust in
The tents of their camp in the field
The storehouses they built for grain

cards.text: Then Moses says something hard to hear. In the siege, people will eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says that in the siege, even the most gentle and refined man among them will refuse to share with his brother, his wife and his surviving children.

cards.text: The most gentle and refined woman among them, so refined she wouldn't set the sole of her foot on the ground, will begrudge her husband, her son and her daughter. For lack of anything else, she will secretly eat the afterbirth and the children she bears.

Then Moses circles back to the if. If they aren't careful to observe all the words of this law and fear the glorious and awesome name of the LORD, extraordinary disasters and lasting plagues will come on them and their descendants.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the LORD will afflict Israel again with the diseases they dreaded in Egypt.
True or false: Moses says the sicknesses will stop at the ones written in the Book of the Law.

cards.text: Then Moses brings up the stars: they were as numerous as the stars in the sky. Friend, I lose count of the sprinkles on ONE cookie, so the stars? Forget it.

cards.question: Because they would not obey the voice of the LORD, Moses says the people once as numerous as the stars will be left ___ in number.

cards.text: Just as it pleased the LORD to make them prosper and multiply, Moses says it will please Him to destroy them. They'll be uprooted from the very land they're about to enter.

cards.question: After Israel is uprooted from the land, where does Moses say the LORD will send them?

cards.text: Out there, Moses says, they'll find no rest, not even a resting place for the sole of their foot, and the LORD will give them a trembling heart, failing eyes and a despairing soul. In the morning they'll say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening, 'If only it were morning!'

cards.question: Wishing away every morning and every evening, Moses says they'll live with ___ in their hearts because of the terrifying sights they will see.

cards.text: Then one last picture. Moses says the LORD will return them to Egypt in ships, by a route they were told they should never see again.

cards.question: Back in Egypt, Moses says Israel will sell themselves to their enemies as male and female slaves. What will happen then?

answers.text: Their enemies will buy them all
